acceptance: Exactly one authoritative v1 schema source exists for the generated core contract and is valid JSON Schema Draft 2020-12. Rust/TypeScript generated outputs declare that source plus exact schema SHA-256.

Generator is deterministic and fail-closed: unsupported schema construct/type/reference fails; two generations from identical input are byte-identical; --check reports clean on the committed candidate and fails on deliberate drift.
Generated Rust and TypeScript expose equivalent provider-neutral type/enum shapes for canonical references, capability/grant, runtime/operation/error, ArtifactRef, Event, and Evidence core messages.
Generated files are derived outputs and contain an explicit do-not-edit header. No critical core wire type is separately hand-maintained in Rust or TypeScript.
Shared fixtures include at least one capability/grant message, one runtime-operation message, and one Event/Evidence message; both languages consume the same tracked fixture bytes.

Rust serde/serde_json fixture tests deserialize and serialize every shared fixture and preserve semantic JSON value equality. TypeScript/Node conformance checks parse every fixture, validate required generated contract shape/schema-supported constraints, and preserve semantic JSON value equality.

Schema/generated contract preserves prior semantic distinctions including UUID/revision references, RequestId versus OperationId, contact versus execution state, side-effect certainty/retry guidance, stream_seq/previous_event_id, Artifact digest binding, Evidence source class, and redaction state.

Provider/donor names are absent from the authoritative core schema and generated public contract identifiers. Foreign provider metadata remains bounded generic diagnostic data only where the semantic contract permits it.
Normal pnpm check covers generator drift plus TypeScript contract/fixture conformance and cargo check covers the Rust contracts/fixtures. Existing CI remains green.
Canonical documentation states JSON Schema 2020-12 as the single source and clearly defers compatibility/unknown-field rules to S05-T02 and the full adversarial corpus to S05-T03.

Exact implementation passes generator determinism/drift checks, shared-fixture Rust+TypeScript conformance, provider-name scan, pnpm check, git diff --check, Diffcipline R2, protected exact-head CI, and post-merge main qualification.

minimality.rationale: Use the existing Node/Rust toolchain and one JSON Schema file with a small in-repo generator; add only serde/serde_json on the Rust side for real JSON round-trip rather than introducing protoc, JVM, an external codegen service, or parallel handwritten contract definitions.

requirements: Generated contracts must not infer authority from successful schema validation; validation proves shape only.
Generated outputs must not be hand-edited or become a competing source of truth.
Unsupported schema constructs fail generation rather than being silently ignored or approximated.
Provider-specific names/types must not enter the canonical core schema or public generated contract API.
Compatibility behavior not frozen by this task must not be guessed into generated validators; defer it explicitly to S05-T02.

outcome: Kernux has one repository-owned JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 source for the v1 core protocol contract, deterministic Rust and TypeScript generated types, shared canonical fixtures, and cross-language round-trip/conformance checks that fail on schema/generated drift.
rationale: P01 semantic contracts S01-S04 are PROVEN. KRP now needs executable cross-language contracts before compatibility rules and the adversarial corpus can be frozen. JSON Schema 2020-12 provides a language-neutral inspectable source without requiring protoc or a second schema compiler, while a deliberately restricted repository-owned subset keeps generation deterministic and auditable.

risk.recovery: Revert schema/generator/generated outputs/fixtures/contracts crate/workspace scripts/ADR and closeout state. No production runtime consumes these generated contracts yet, so no persisted-data or wire migration is required.

scope_in: Select JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 as the single authoritative v1 cross-language schema source under protocol/schema. Generated Rust and TypeScript files must identify the source path and exact schema SHA-256 and must not be hand-edited.

Define a deliberately restricted JSON Schema subset sufficient for P01 core protocol types: definitions, object, string, integer, boolean, arrays, string enums, local references, required properties, descriptions, patterns, numeric bounds, and additionalProperties=false. Unsupported schema constructs fail generation explicitly.
Create a deterministic repository-local Node generator with no runtime network dependency. Same schema bytes must produce byte-identical Rust and TypeScript generated outputs.

Generate provider-neutral Rust and TypeScript contract types for canonical refs, capability requests/grants, runtime negotiation/operation observation/errors, Artifact refs, Event envelope, and Evidence records while preserving S01-S04 semantic field distinctions.
Use serde/serde_json for Rust JSON fixture round-trip and standard JSON plus TypeScript compile-time types/check helpers for TypeScript. Lock exact Rust dependency resolution in Cargo.lock.
Create one shared fixture directory consumed by both Rust and TypeScript conformance tests. At minimum include representative capability/grant, runtime-operation, and Event/Evidence envelopes.
Add deterministic generation drift checking: protocol generation in --check mode must fail when committed generated output differs from schema-derived output.

Add cross-language round-trip checks: each shared fixture validates against the supported schema subset/source contract, deserializes and reserializes in Rust, is parsed/shape-checked in TypeScript/Node, and preserves semantic JSON value equality after canonical object-key-insensitive comparison.
Add a generated-contract smoke surface to normal pnpm check and Cargo workspace CI without weakening existing gates.
Add an accepted ADR recording JSON Schema 2020-12, generated-output ownership, and the restricted-subset rule. Align PROTOCOL_STRATEGY and development documentation.
Prove generated core contracts contain no provider-specific names or donor-specific public types.
scope_out: Do not define final unknown/additive-field compatibility or version-negotiation policy; KX-P01-S05-T02 owns it.
Do not build the full negative/adversarial protocol fixture corpus for disconnect, duplicate operation, malformed payload, and version mismatch; KX-P01-S05-T03 owns it.
Do not implement kernuxd, transport, persistence, event store, runtime adapters, browser/process execution, or UI.
Do not make JSON Schema validation itself an authorization boundary; S02/S03 kernel semantics remain authoritative.
title: KX-P01-S05-T01 — Select JSON Schema source and generate Rust/TypeScript protocol contracts
